_comment: Catching and orbs. ALL of it is TUNABLE. M3 exists to answer one question: does landing a good throw feel satisfying? The expected feedback is 'catching is too hard', 'aiming is fiddly', 'I never know if I was close' — every one of those has to be answerable by editing this file.
_comment_model: Throwing hands camera and control to the trainer for a real-time over-the-shoulder aim (docs/decisions/D08). Your creature is undefended while you aim and the opponent does not stop attacking it. That cost is the whole design: it is what makes throwing a decision rather than something you spam between attacks.

chance._comment: catch_chance = species_rate * hp_factor * orb_multiplier * accuracy_bonus, clamped. Nothing is ever certain and nothing that is legal is ever impossible; a throw that cannot succeed should be REFUSED with a reason, not rolled at zero.
chance._comment_hp: GAME_DESIGN.md 15: full-health throws are allowed, and powerful/full-health creatures should be extremely difficult to catch. So this curve is steep. At full health you are multiplying the species rate by 0.10; at a sliver you are multiplying by 1.0.
chance._comment_curve: Exponent on the (1 - hp_fraction) term. Above 1 the reward is back-loaded, so chipping a creature down to half does much less for you than taking it to a sliver — which is what keeps 'damage it first' a real risk against 'over-damage it and lose the catch'. TUNABLE, retuned 1.6 -> 1.2 for OF19: the endpoints (hp_factor_full/empty) are untouched by this exponent, so full-health throws stay exactly as hard as before — only the middle of the curve moves, so a realistic 'brought it to about half, didn't risk a faint' throw stops being punished almost as hard as a full-health one.
chance._comment_accuracy: How much a good throw is worth. `centre_bonus` applies to a dead-centre hit, `edge_bonus` to one that barely clipped. This is the ONLY reason the aiming skill exists; if these are equal, aiming is decoration and the milestone has no subject. TUNABLE, edge_bonus nudged 0.75 -> 0.80 for OF19: a clipped-but-landed hit (the realistic outcome on a handheld when the throw itself is hard to read) was being penalised almost as hard as a whiff, on top of orb.gd's own miss case for throws that never reach the body at all. centre_bonus stays put so a dead-centre throw is still clearly worth more (1.45 vs 0.80) — aiming still matters.

orbs._comment: Orb types. GAME_DESIGN.md 15: basic orbs should be affordable enough that players are encouraged to try, and never so scarce that they are afraid to experiment; better orbs are meaningful crafting/progression rewards. Every key here IS the real satchel item id (data/items/items.json) -- catch_math.gd's best_orb()/orb_ids() read this table directly rather than translating between a tier name and an item id, so adding a tier is one entry in one file.
orbs._comment_greater: R4.9: the tier ladder's first rung. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md Band 2 names 'improved Orb tier' as the first thing Rootstone (SD18) buys -- R4.9 built the mechanic and the item; SD18 (data/recipes/recipes_rootstone.json's `orb_greater` recipe) closed the remainder by adding the recipe that actually lets a player craft one, from Rootstone plus wood and fiber. Multiplier is TUNABLE, not load-bearing: comfortably better without being 'just throw this and it's basically a catch' -- that would make the basic tier feel like a mistake to ever use, which is its own kind of failure per GAME_DESIGN.md 15's affordability rule.
orbs._comment_stock: RETIRED as a live value: orbs are satchel items now (data/items/items.json), spent by throw_aim.gd from the real inventory, and Grandpa's opening gift is the starting supply (data/dialogue/opening.json give: effects). Kept only so catch_math.starting_stock() keeps answering for anything historical; nothing refills from it.

throw._comment: The projectile. A real arc, not a hitscan — GAME_DESIGN.md 15 forbids throwing without player aim, and an instant hit gives nothing to aim.
throw._comment_radius: Collision radius of the orb in metres. The FIRST lever to reach for if aiming feels fiddly on the handheld: widen this before touching anything else, because it forgives the input without removing the skill. TUNABLE, widened 0.42 -> 0.60 for OF19 (owner report: 'too hard to know where the ball is going to go') — orb.gd's own hit test is body_radius + this radius, so this is pure forgiveness on the miss/no-miss line and does not touch accuracy_bonus's centre/edge scoring at all.
throw._comment_windup: Seconds between committing to the throw and the orb leaving the trainer's hand. Short — the commitment already happened when you entered aim mode.
throw._comment_lockout: Seconds after a throw resolves before another can be started. Stops a failed catch from being instantly re-thrown while the wobble is still on screen.

aim._comment: The over-the-shoulder aim camera, expressed as a camera_rig profile. Reuses scripts/player/camera_rig.gd's set_target(target, profile) rather than adding a third camera — the same reasoning that deleted combat_camera.gd in M2.
aim._comment_distance: Far enough back that the trainer does not fill the frame. At 2.4m their body covered the whole view and the reticle sat on their shoulder — you were aiming at your own trainer.
aim._comment_shoulder: Wide, because in aim mode the trainer is close to the lens and would otherwise sit on top of the reticle. The orb is thrown at whatever the reticle is over rather than parallel to the camera, so this offset does not put the throw somewhere other than where you aimed.
aim._comment_sensitivity: Aiming wants a slower stick than looking around does. This scales the rig's normal gamepad sensitivity while aim mode is active. (It was written on day one and read by nothing until the throw-feel pass — the aim ran at full exploration turn rate, which was most of 'aiming is fiddly'.)
aim._comment_response: Exponent on stick deflection while aiming. Above 1 gives a slow, precise centre without costing full-deflection speed. Tunable.
aim._comment_near: Extra sensitivity scale while the reticle is over the creature, so the last degrees of a line-up do not overshoot. Tunable.
aim._comment_guard: Seconds of input ignored on entering aim mode, so the press that opens the aim is not also read as the release.

resolve._comment: The wobble. The outcome is DECIDED ONCE when the orb lands and the shakes are derived from it — they never re-roll. Tension built on a lie is what makes catch animations feel cheap, and a wobble that can contradict the result already computed is exactly that lie. ALL timing here is TUNABLE; the sequence is: strike flash -> absorb -> the orb drops and settles -> first_shake_delay of stillness -> shakes at shake_interval -> settle_pause of held breath -> verdict.
resolve._comment_failure: A near miss shakes more times before breaking out than a hopeless one, so the wobble count is honest information about how close the throw was.
resolve._comment_absorb: Seconds the creature takes to be drawn into the orb after the strike. The orb hangs at the strike point for exactly this long before dropping, so the creature always shrinks toward a stationary orb.
resolve._comment_first_shake: Seconds of dead stillness between the orb coming to rest and the first shake. This is the dread beat — cutting it to zero makes the wobble start before the eye has settled on the orb.
resolve._comment_interval: Seconds from the start of one shake to the start of the next. Was 0.55, which read as a metronome; the orb's own rock animation is ~0.45s, so anything under ~0.7 leaves no stillness between shakes and stillness is where the tension lives.
resolve._comment_settle: Seconds of held breath between the last shake and the verdict. (This key existed before and was silently ignored — the verdict landed on the same frame as the final shake, which is exactly the beat a catch sequence cannot skip.)
resolve._comment_breakout: Seconds the creature takes to pop back out of a failed catch, scaling up with an overshoot.

resolve_camera._comment: camera_rig profile for the wobble: a close-up on the resting orb, entered with a slow glide (retarget_lag) the moment the orb strikes. The whole resolution plays through this shot — the orb is the only actor on stage and the camera says so. Handed back to the creature on a breakout and to the trainer when a catch ends the fight.
resolve_camera._comment_framing: First capture at distance 3.2 / height 1.1 / pitch -16 was not a close-up at all: the orb huddled small at the bottom of the frame with dead grass in the centre. Height near the orb itself and a steeper look-down centre it.

vfx._comment: The three flashes of a catch, all impact_flash.gd bursts (primitives, both renderers, physics clock). Strike says 'you hit it'; caught is the warm gold seal; breakout is a sharper, whiter burst so failure never reads as the success flash with different text.
vfx._comment_sizes: Sized against the resolve close-up, not the combat camera: at radius 1.5+ under strength 1.3+ the verdict bursts filled half the frame and washed the creature and orb out of their own moment.

faint._comment: GAME_DESIGN.md 15: over-damaging a creature and causing a faint ends the capture opportunity, and fainted wild creatures remain visible temporarily but cannot be captured. The lingering body is not decoration — it is what makes the lost chance legible instead of the creature simply vanishing.

aggression._comment: Aggressive wild creatures, per GAME_DESIGN.md pillar 3 and 14 ('Aggressive creature initiates'). The 'not simple proximity' rule in 14 is scoped to PEACEFUL creatures; these are the other kind. Deliberately thin: notice, close, initiate. No stalking, no growl phase, no standing your ground — those are a behaviour system and this is a flag and a chase.
aggression._comment_engage: Metres at which it forces the fight. Under the peaceful engage_range so you cannot be ambushed from further away than you could have chosen to fight from.
aggression._comment_giveup: Metres from its home beyond which it loses interest and walks back. Without this an aggressive creature follows you across the whole meadow and the only escape is a fight.
aggression._comment_grace: Seconds after a fight ends before it will come at you again. Being re-engaged the instant you win is not danger, it is a soft lock.
